BILL NUMBER:  S2303

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the
public officers law, in relation to authorizing local authorities to
establish demonstration programs, implementing railroad grade crossing
monitoring systems by means of photo devices

 PURPOSE :

This bill would allow any local authority to adopt a local law to
implement a program to install and operate railroad grade crossing
photo violation-monitoring devices at any railroad sign or signal.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new section
135-a to define railroad grade crossing as a location where railroad
tracks intersect a public or private highway, roadway or sidewalk.

Section two amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new section
1170-a to establish a demonstration program imposing monetary
liability on the owner of a vehicle for failure of an operator to
comply with section eleven hundred seventy of this article regarding
obedience to signal indicating approach of train. The liability of the
owner shall not exceed one hundred dollars for each violation;
however, the adjudicating authority may provide for an additional
penalty not in excess of twenty-five dollars for each violation for
the failure to respond to a notice of liability within the prescribed
period of time

The demonstration program will utilize necessary technologies to
ensure that photographs produced by such railroad grade crossing photo
violation-monitoring systems shall not include images that identify
the driver, the passengers or the contents of the vehicle.  However, a
notice of liability will not be dismissed solely because a
photograph(s) allows for the identification of the contents of a
vehicle.

Furthermore, notices of liability are not deemed a conviction as an
operator, so they would result in no points on the owner's driver
license, nor are they used for motor vehicle insurance purposes. The
bill specifies the procedure required to provide notices of liability
to the owner of the vehicle, as well as the required information
contained on the notices. It shall be a defense to liability that the
vehicle was reported to police as stolen prior to the time the
violation occurred, and that the railroad signal indications were
malfunctioning at the time of the alleged violation.

Additionally, any local authority which adopts a demonstration program
must submit an annual report on the result of the use of a railroad
grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system to the governor, the
temporary president of the senate and the speaker of the assembly on
or before June 1, 2019, and on the same date in each succeeding year
the program is operable. The report must include, but is not limited
to, the following: a description of the locations where railroad grade
crossing photo violation-monitoring systems were used; the number,
type and severity of accidents reported at intersections where a
railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system is used for
the year preceding the installation of the system; the number, type
and severity of accidents reported at the intersections where a
railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system is used; the
number of violations recorded at each intersection where a railroad
grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system is used and in the
aggregate on a daily, weekly and monthly basis; the total number of
notices of liability issued for violations recorded by the system; the
number of fines and total amount of fines paid after first notice of
liability issued for violations recorded by such system; the number of
violations adjudicated and result of such adjudications including
breakdowns of dispositions made for violations recorded by such
systems; the total amount of revenue realized by such local authority
from such adjudications; expenses incurred by such local authority in
connection with the program; and quality of the adjudication process
and its results.

Section three amends the public officers law to state that the
photographs, microphotographs, videotapes or other recorded images
prepared by the railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring
system may not be subject to FOIL requests.

Section four establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

According to Federal Railroad Administration data, accidents at
railroad grade crossings have decreased over the past decade, except
within the borders of the Empire State. Federal data documents that
from 2004-2014 there have been 371 collisions resulting in 63 deaths
and 137 injuries. In 2013 alone there were a total of 28 accidents on
the state's three most prominent commuter rail lines. It has become
increasingly apparent that there is a substantial need for increased
safety measures at railroad grade crossings in the state.

In February of 2015, a northbound Metro-North Railroad passenger train
collided with a sports utility vehicle which had stopped on the
tracks. This tragic accident resulted in the deaths of five passengers
and the driver of the vehicle. The presence of warning devices such as
flashing lights, signs and gates have helped to reduce the number of
catastrophes such as the February crash, but have failed to adequately
deter drivers from failing to adhere to these crucial safety measures.

Additionally, on May 4, 2015, a school bus at Roaring Brook Road
railroad crossing in Westchester County stopped only inches from the
tracks leaving just enough clearance from the passing train to avoid
an accident; however, the driver failed to leave enough room for the
lowering gate causing the bus to become trapped. Since March 2014,
there were thirty-eight tickets issued at this specific crossing for
driving violations. These near miss situations bring much needed
attention to the fact that aggressive or distracted drivers are
failing to comply with safety laws at railroad grade crossings.

This piece of legislation would aid in the effort to decrease the
incidences of vehicular accidents at railroad grade crossings by
providing a mechanism, at the local authorities' option, to deter
driving violations which result in these horrific and costly
collisions. Utilizing the same technology as red light cameras,
railroad grade crossing violation-monitoring systems will fine drivers
who fail to adhere to safety signals indicating an approaching train.
This will incentivize drivers to pay particular attention to signs
indicating appropriate stopping distances from railroad crossings and
thereby prevent serious and deadly accidents.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-2016: S.5238A - Unanimously passed the Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the state

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This law shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law.

BILL NUMBER:  S2303A

public officers law, in relation to authorizing political subdivisions
and commuter railroads to establish demonstration programs,

photo devices

 PURPOSE :

This bill would authorize political subdivisions and commuter
railroads to establish a demonstration program to install and operate
railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring devices at railroad
signs or signals within their jurisdiction.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new section
1170-a to establish a demonstration program imposing monetary
liability on the owner of a vehicle for failure of an operator to
comply with section eleven hundred seventy of this article regarding
obedience to signal indicating approach of train. The demonstration
program will empower a political subdivision to install and operate
railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring devices at any
railroad sign or signal within its jurisdiction. The cost of the
devices will be borne by the political subdivision, a commuter
railroad operating in the political subdivision, or a combination of
both through a memorandum of understanding. The owner liable for a
violation of § 1170 of the Vehicle and Traffic law will be liable for
monetary penalties not to exceed $250 for each violation.
Adjudication of liability will be by the court having jurisdiction
over traffic infractions.

Furthermore, notices of liability are not deemed a conviction as an
operator, so they would result in no points on the owner's driver
license, nor are they used for motor vehicle insurance purposes. It
shall be a defense to liability that the vehicle was reported to
police as stolen prior to the time the violation occurred, and an
affirmative defense that the railroad signal indications were
malfunctioning at the time of the alleged violation.

Additionally, any local authority which adopts a demonstration program
must submit an annual report on the result of the use of a railroad
grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system to the governor, the
temporary president of the senate and the speaker of the assembly on
or before June 1, 2019, and on the same date in each succeeding year
the program is operable. The report must include, but is not limited
to, the following: a description of the locations where railroad grade
crossing photo violation-monitoring systems were used; the number,
type and severity of accidents reported at intersections where a
railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system is used for
the year preceding the installation of the system; the number, type
and severity of accidents reported at the intersections where a
railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system is used; the
number of violations recorded at each intersection where a railroad
grade crossing photo violation-monitoring system is used and in the
aggregate on a daily, weekly and monthly basis; the total number of
notices of liability issued for violations recorded by the system; the
number of fines and total amount of fines paid after first notice of
liability issued for violations recorded by such system; the number of
violations adjudicated and result of such adjudications including
breakdowns of dispositions made for violations recorded by such
systems; the total amount of revenue realized by such local authority
from such adjudications; expenses incurred by such local authority in
connection with the program; and quality of the adjudication process
and its results.
Section two amends the vehicle and traffic law by added a new section
1633 regarding railroad grade crossing enforcement of the
demonstration program. These provisions authorize the MTA to implement
this demonstration program. This authorizing language provides the
same provisions established in section one that are applicable to
political subdivisions.

Section three amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 1 of section
1803 of the vehicle and traffic law regarding disposition of fines and
forfeitures to include newly established section 1633 of the vehicle
and traffic law.

Section four amends section 1803 of the vehicle and traffic law by
adding a new subdivision 10 to state that where a commuter railroad
establishes a railroad grade-crossing demonstration program, all
fines, penalties and forfeitures collected will be paid to the city,
village, town or suburban town having jurisdiction of the railroad
grade crossing.

Section five amends the public officers law to state that the
photographs, microphotographs, videotapes or other recorded images
prepared by the railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring
system may not be subject to FOIL requests.

Section six establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

According to Federal Railroad Administration data, accidents at
railroad grade crossings have decreased over the past decade, except
within the borders of the Empire State. Federal data documents that
from 2004-2014 there have been 371 collisions resulting in 63 deaths
and 137 injuries. In 2013 alone there were a total of 28 accidents on
the state's three most prominent commuter rail lines. It has become
increasingly apparent that there is a substantial need for increased
safety measures at railroad grade crossings in the state.

In February of 2015, a northbound Metro-North Railroad passenger train
collided with a sports utility vehicle which had stopped on the
tracks. This tragic accident resulted in the deaths of five passengers
and the driver of the vehicle. The presence of warning devices such as
flashing lights, signs and gates have helped to reduce the number of
catastrophes such as the February crash, but have failed to adequately
deter drivers from failing to adhere to these crucial safety measures.

Additionally, on May 4, 2015, a school bus at Roaring Brook Road
railroad crossing in Westchester County stopped only inches from the
tracks leaving just enough clearance from the passing train to avoid
an accident; however, the driver failed to leave enough room for the
lowering gate causing the bus to become trapped. Since March 2014,
there were thirty-eight tickets issued at this specific crossing for
driving violations. These near miss situations bring much needed
attention to the fact that aggressive or distracted drivers are
failing to comply with safety laws at railroad grade crossings.

This piece of legislation would aid in the effort to decrease the
incidences of vehicular accidents at railroad grade crossings by
providing a mechanism for municipalities and the commuter railroad to
deter driving violations, which result in these horrific and costly
collisions. Utilizing the same technology as red light cameras,
railroad grade crossing violation-monitoring systems will fine drivers
who fail to adhere to safety signals indicating an approaching train.
This will incentivize drivers to pay particular attention to signs
indicating appropriate stopping distances from railroad crossings and
thereby prevent serious and deadly accidents.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-2016: S.5238A - Unanimously passed the Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This law shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law.
